page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.24xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized, GPU-accelerated virtual machine powered by KVM virtualization. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor providing 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem features 33 MB of L3 cache alongside support for instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, BMI2, and FMA. Accompanying the processor is 736 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 7.67 GB of memory per physical core.

Hardware acceleration is driven by eight dedicated NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs, supplying a combined 256 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM with 32 GB per accelerator. The instance does not include local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of network-based block storage volumes for persistent data. For network I/O, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned complimentary by default.

In synthetic processing evaluations, the instance demonstrates distinct architectural behaviors. The stress-ng multi-core CPU benchmark achieved a score of 70674.73, placing it within the upper tier of tested systems due to its high parallel core count. Conversely, single-core performance recorded a stress-ng score of 1104.49, falling into the lower quartile. This variance highlights that the platform is engineered primarily for massively parallelized operations rather than single-threaded clock speed efficiency.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the substantial footprint of eight high-capacity accelerators and 736 GB of memory represents a high-density, enterprise-grade investment. It minimizes operational overhead for clustered computing by packaging extensive GPU compute and VRAM capacity into a single node. The server is well aligned for distributed deep learning training, high-performance computing (HPC) simulations, large-scale video processing, and parallel scientific workloads requiring extensive GPU acceleration and large host memory pools.

This configuration favors multi-threaded parallelism over single-core speed. With its high density of compute and accelerator resources, the instance suits demanding workloads including distributed deep learning model training, AI inference clusters, and complex scientific simulations.
